issues.source_quote: Они могут его распилить, переплавить и даже продать за границу.
issues.translation_quote: They can saw it up, melt it down, even sell it abroad.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the earlier 'Тики так' being rendered 'Ticky-tack' while the gloss scene says 'Хорошо? - Тики-так' is fine; however the key joke 'Тики так' is kept as an opaque nonsense word with no cue to its slang meaning.

issues.translation_quote: Yes, yes. IRS.
issues.justification: ОБХС is the Soviet anti-embezzlement police; 'IRS' is an anachronistic, wrong-culture equivalent, and the joke (thief mishearing 'yes' as police) is lost.

issues.translation_quote: I'll rip your jaws! ... gouge your peepers out!
issues.justification: 'Rip your jaws' is a stiff calque of the idiom 'пасть порву' (rip your mouth/maw); it sounds unnatural and weakens the thug voice, though it is used consistently.

issues.translation_quote: A bad person? - A radish.
issues.justification: 'Редиска' as thieves' slang for a rotten person is rendered literally, so the slang gloss reads as nonsense; the later 'Radish - a bad person' scene still works, but the humor of the 'dictionary' exchange is weakened.

issues.translation_quote: Push bull.
issues.justification: 'Push bull' is not a natural English phrase; the thieves' slang for lying is lost.

issues.translation_quote: - Good? - Ticky-tack.
issues.justification: The word means 'okay/fine' in the thieves' jargon; 'ticky-tack' in English means cheap/tacky, creating a misleading connotation.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк... Я злой и страшный серый волк, я в поросятах знаю толк.
issues.translation_quote: Who's afraid of the big bad wolf... I'm the big bad wolf, so grim and gruff, and piglets? Oh, I know my stuff!
issues.justification: Acceptable adaptation, but the rhyme in the second line is awkward ('and piglets? Oh, I know my stuff') and it's a substituted Western reference for a Soviet cartoon song.

issues.source_quote: - Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: Those two are doing time in Central Asia, and he's near Moscow.
issues.justification: Earlier the translation says 'got 4 years each' for the others; fine. But 'Kindergarten' scene: 'Вр оде' rendered 'Sort of' loses the ironic confirmation; minor.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший ты человек, Косой, злой, как собака.
issues.translation_quote: You bad man, Squint, mean like dog.
issues.justification: Broken pidgin English is used for Vasya in places where he speaks ordinary (if colloquial) Russian, e.g. 'Чегой-то ты воруешь', 'Хмырь повесился' passages ('Why you so mean? Why like dog?'), 'I mangy jackal'. This imposes a foreign-speaker voice inconsistent with source, where only the Central Asian character's deliberate pidgin jokes ('Гражданина, ты туда не ходи') are marked.

issues.source_quote: Лодочной станции... В проруби. Косой, плавать умеешь?
issues.translation_quote: By the boat station... In the ice hole. Squint, can you swim?
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Косой' as 'Squint' versus the character 'Косой' in other places is consistent; however 'Хмыренок' → 'Little Khmyr' and 'Хмырь' left untranslated while others are translated creates inconsistent nickname treatment.

issues.translation_quote: Swim where? In this freezing cold?

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии
issues.translation_quote: Those two are doing time in Central Asia

issues.source_quote: Пасть, пасть... - Доцент, ты был когда-нибудь маленький?
issues.translation_quote: - Jaws, jaws... - Docent, were you ever little?
Fitness salute!
issues.justification: The Soviet-era catchphrase greeting is rendered with a stiff, unnatural calque that fails to convey the jokey sports-greeting.

issues.translation_quote: the Three Poplars on Plyushchikha
issues.justification: A culturally specific reference to a famous Soviet film (Three Poplars on Plyushchikha) is left opaque to the English audience with no cue; the joke about standing in plain sight is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Ну ты даешь! ... Ну, а я знаю? ... Ну ты даешь! Кто же его посадит? Он же памятник!
issues.translation_quote: You're something else! Who'd ever put him inside? He's a monument!
issues.justification: The pun on 'сидит/посадит' (sitting vs. imprisoning) is lost: 'put him inside' does not mirror the double meaning set up by 'Is he seated?', so the joke fails.

issues.source_quote: - Елка, что ли? - Сам ты елка!
issues.translation_quote: - A fir tree, or what? - You're a fir tree!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but 'елка' as an insult for a fool is lost; reads flat.

issues.source_quote: Против бритвы - пиджак и брюки. Только пиджак.
issues.translation_quote: Against the razor - jacket and trousers. - Just the jacket.
Ears, ears, ears!
issues.justification: Chess-game banter loses the colloquial comedic tone; 'Ears' is a literal rendering of a playful cry.

issues.source_quote: Можно просто так посидеть, поговорить по душам. А я не прокурор, чтоб с тобой по душам разговаривать.
issues.translation_quote: We could just sit and have a heart-to-heart. I'm no prosecutor to have heart-to-hearts with you.

issues.source_quote: Я говорю "Москва", а ты на последнюю букву "А" - Астрахань.
issues.translation_quote: I say "Moscow" - "Moskva," and you take the last letter, "A" - Astrakhan.
issues.justification: The word game only works with Russian names; the translation awkwardly retains Russian city names and adds 'Moskva' as a fix, which is clumsy but conveys the idea.

issues.translation_quote: No helmet.
Those two
not-nice person / bad person

issues.source_quote: Тебя сегодня как с лестницы башкой скинули, - так тебе и вторая половина отказала.
issues.translation_quote: When they threw you down the stairs head first today, - your other half quit on you too.
issues.justification: The original implies his other half of the memory/brain also failed (both halves of the head); 'your other half' is vague and the joke is muddled.

issues.source_quote: Это не смешно, тетя. - Не смешно.
issues.translation_quote: - That's not funny, lady. - Not funny.
It's gone. Was here, now it's not.
A gentleman of fortune!
issues.justification: Acceptable; the film's title phrase is rendered idiomatically.

issues.source_quote: Девушка? - Чувиха. - Да нет, по-английски, ну? Герл!
issues.translation_quote: - Girl? - Chick. - No, in English, come on! Girl! - Oh, yes, girl!
What are you hollering for?

issues.source_quote: Рябого бритвой по горлу - чик и приветик
issues.translation_quote: snick, and bye-bye

issues.source_quote: Пошли! Здесь у нас будет игротека... - а вот здесь будет спортзал.
issues.translation_quote: Here we'll have a playroom...
Yeah, done. Checkmate.
You need to take the best spot.
Fedya Yermakov

issues.source_quote: Гениально! Ведь родная мать не отличит кто есть кто!
issues.translation_quote: Brilliant! Your own mother couldn't tell who's who!

issues.source_quote: Это тебе не мелочь по карманам тырить!
issues.translation_quote: This ain't pinching pocket change!
No more picture show. Electricity's all used up.
issues.justification: The famous catchphrase from Central Asian film screenings ('Кина не будет') is rendered with an odd, flat English version that loses the cultural and comic flavor.

issues.translation_quote: We drank. Shut up!

issues.source_quote: Хоть бы записку оставил, когда вешался.
issues.translation_quote: Could've at least left a note when you hanged yourself.
We give uuup... Already shaved!
issues.justification: The final punchline about 'already shaved' (having heads shaved in prison) is left ambiguous and falls flat.
